entry.translit: kannᵉlōṯᵉḵā; ʾōsep̄ he-ḥāsîl; kᵉmaššaq gēḇîm šôqēq; ʾĕmûnaṯ ʿittêḵā; ḥōsen; ʾerʾellām; malʾăḵê šālôm; kāʿărāḇāh; nōʿēr; yāḡûr; môqᵉḏê ʿôlām; sōp̄ēr; šōqēl; nôʿāz; qiryaṯ môʿăḏēnû; nāweh šaʾănān; ḥăḇālāyw; mᵉḥōqᵉqēnû; ḥăḇālayiḵ; ʿaḏ-šālāl; bāzᵉzû baz
entry.strongs: H5239 or H3615 (nlh / klh, 33:1); H2625 (ḥāsîl); H4944 (maššāq); H8264 (šqq); H530 (ʾĕmûnāh); H2633 (ḥōsen); H691 (ʾerʾēl); H4397 (malʾāḵ); H6160 (ʿărāḇāh); H5287 (nʿr); H1481 (gûr); H4168 (môqēḏ); H5608 (sōp̄ēr); H8254 (šāqal); H5810 (ʿāzaz 'be strong, be insolent', the root the 33:19 note and ASV/JPS 1917 'fierce' assume for the single-occurrence nôʿāz; some concordances list the form under H3267 yāʿaz); H4150 (môʿēḏ); H5116 (nāweh); H7600 (šaʾănān); H2256 (ḥeḇel); H2710 (ḥāqaq); H5706 (ʿaḏ 'prey'); H957 (baz); H962 (bāzaz). Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entry.lemma: single-site lexical and textual decisions of Isaiah 33 not covered by a dedicated entry
entry.literal: when you finish(?); the gathering of the locust; like the rushing of locusts, one rushing; firmness of your times; store; their heroes(?); messengers of peace; like the desert; shaking off; will sojourn; burnings of perpetuity; one counting; one weighing; insolent(?); city of our appointed times; untroubled pasture-abode; its cords; your cords; prey of spoil; they plundered plunder
entry.standardEnglish: ASV: 'when thou hast made an end of dealing treacherously'; 'as the caterpillar gathereth: as locusts leap shall men leap upon it'; 'stability in thy times, abundance of salvation'; 'their valiant ones'; 'the ambassadors of peace'; 'like a desert'; 'shake off [their leaves]'; 'dwell … everlasting burnings'; 'he that counted … he that weighed [the tribute]'; 'the fierce people'; 'the city of our solemnities'; 'a quiet habitation'; 'the cords thereof'; 'our lawgiver'; 'Thy tacklings are loosed'; 'the prey of a great spoil'; 'the lame took the prey'. JPS 1917 and NJPS as cited in the chapter commentary (all three checked 2026-11-26).
entry.wohChoice: ASV wording kept except where the book's concordance requires a change. Kept: 33:1 'when you have made an end of dealing treacherously' (klh reading; JPS 1917 'weary' = lʾh in commentary); 33:4 'as the caterpillar gathers; as locusts leap, so they leap upon it' (indefinite 'they' for ASV's supplied 'men'; future tense with ASV); 33:6 'stability in your times, an abundance of salvation'; 33:7 MT ʾerʾellām 'their valiant ones' (NJPS 'the Arielites' and the repointing 'I will appear to them' in commentary); 33:9 'like a desert' (common noun, as 35:1, 6; 40:3) and 'shake off their leaves' (object supplied as in ASV); 33:14 gûr 'dwell' (as 11:6; 'sojourn' at 16:4 and 23:7 for a stay abroad) and 'everlasting burnings'; 33:18 'the one who counted … the one who weighed' (participle, no supplied object); 33:19 'the fierce people'; 33:20 'the city of our appointed feasts' (môʿăḏîm as 1:14) and 'a quiet habitation' (šaʾănān 'quiet' as 32:18; 'peaceful' stays for nᵉwēh šālôm 32:18); 33:22 'our judge … our lawgiver … our king'. Changed: 33:7 malʾăḵê šālôm 'the messengers of peace' (malʾāḵ 'messenger' as 14:32; 18:2; 42:19; 44:26; ASV 'ambassadors'); 33:20 and 33:23 ḥeḇel 'cords' in both verses (ASV 'tacklings' at 33:23); 33:23 baz 'plunder' in the cognate object 'the lame took the plunder' (šālāl 'spoil' / baz 'plunder' as 10:6; ASV 'prey' for both ʿaḏ and baz).
entry.rationale: Isaiah 33 is a liturgy built from short, compressed clauses, and several of its words are rare (kannᵉlōṯᵉḵā, ʾerʾellām, nôʿāz and yiṣʿān are found only here) or uncertain in every version; NJPS marks vv. 4, 6 and 23 'Meaning of Heb. uncertain'. The entry keeps ASV's reading wherever it translates MT and departs from it only where ASV's English would hide a distinction the book draws elsewhere. malʾāḵ is rendered 'messenger(s)' at every Isaiah site translated so far (14:32; 18:2, where ṣîrîm is 'envoys'; 30:4 draft; 42:19; 44:26); 37:36 and 63:9 are not bound by this choice. So 'ambassadors' at 33:7 would give one noun two English words without a lexical reason. ḥeḇel is the same noun in 33:20 (the tent's cords) and 33:23 (the ship's rigging), and the passage turns on the contrast between cords that will not snap and cords that hang slack, so the line uses 'cords' twice; 'tacklings' (ASV, JPS 1917) and 'ropes' (NJPS) would separate them. bāzᵉzû baz is a cognate accusative, and the book renders baz 'plunder' beside šālāl 'spoil' at 10:6; ASV's 'took the prey' gives baz the word it also uses for ʿaḏ in the same verse. Every rendering is a standard lexical gloss (BDB; HALOT; recalled); most are the wording of at least one of ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS, and the three concordance changes are argued above, so the claim is direct. Readings not taken (JPS 1917 'weary' at 33:1, NJPS 'the Arielites' at 33:7, NJPS 'throat' at 33:18, NJPS 'barbarian' at 33:19) are reported in commentary with their source.

entry.translit: ʾaddîr (33:21 ʾaddîr YHWH lānû; ṣî ʾaddîr; 10:34 bᵉʾaddîr)
entry.strongs: H117 (ʾaddîr); root ʾdr 'be wide, great, majestic' (H142). Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entry.partOfSpeech: adjective, also used as a noun
entry.standardEnglish: ASV 'in majesty' and 'gallant [ship]' (33:21), 'a mighty one' (10:34); JPS 1917 'in majesty' and 'gallant ship' (33:21); NJPS 'in His greatness' and 'mighty craft' (33:21) (checked 2026-11-26)
entry.wohChoice: 'mighty' for ʾaddîr in Isaiah: 33:21 'there YHWH will be mighty for us … and no mighty ship shall pass'; 10:34 'by a mighty one' (stable, already so printed). Never 'majesty' or 'majestic', which the book reserves for the root gʾh (gāʾôn, gēʾûṯ); never 'glorious', reserved for kāḇôḏ.
entry.rationale: ʾaddîr is 'great, mighty, majestic' (BDB; HALOT; recalled), said of waters (Exod 15:10), kings (Ps 136:18), nobles (Jer 14:3) and of YHWH (Ps 8:2, 10; 93:4). ASV renders the two occurrences in Isa 33:21 by two different English words, 'majesty' and 'gallant', so an English reader cannot see that the verse sets the might of YHWH against the 'mighty' ships that cannot cross the waters he becomes; NJPS keeps 'mighty' for the second. The wave I-5 rulings reserve 'majesty' for gāʾôn of God (overlays hadar-splendor-isaiah, gaon-pride-human-arrogance-isaiah, geut-majesty-isaiah), so ASV's first rendering is not available here, and the stable 10:34 already prints ʾaddîr 'a mighty one'. 'Mighty' is a standard lexical gloss, used by NJPS in this verse, and carries no interpretive load, so the claim is direct. Cost recorded: 'mighty' also renders gibbôr in the fixed title 'Mighty God' (9:5; 10:21) and in 'mighty men'; the two words never meet in one verse, and the overlap is accepted. 'Mighty One' also renders ʾăḇîr in the title ʾăḇîr yiśrāʾēl / yaʿăqōḇ (1:24 stable; 49:26; 60:16); the roots do not share a verse. Orchestrator: ISA-10:34 is in a stable chapter; its English line is unchanged, and its glossaryRefs need this id when the diff is merged.

entry.translit: yōp̄î (33:17 bᵉyop̄yô 'in his beauty'; 3:24 taḥaṯ yōp̄î 'instead of beauty')
entry.strongs: H3308 (yōp̄î); root yph 'be beautiful' (H3302). Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entry.standardEnglish: 'beauty' (ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS at 33:17, all checked 2026-11-26; ASV 'beauty' at 3:24)
entry.wohChoice: 'beauty' for yōp̄î: 33:17 'the king in his beauty'; 3:24 'branding instead of beauty' (stable, already so printed). The English word is shared with ṣᵉḇî (overlay tsevi-beauty-isaiah); the sharing is recorded here and in that entry. If a later site puts yōp̄î and ṣᵉḇî in one verse, its Editor must separate them ('loveliness' or 'fairness' for yōp̄î is the recorded fallback).
entry.rationale: yōp̄î is the abstract noun of yph 'be beautiful', the ordinary Hebrew word for beauty of person or thing (Ezek 16:14; 28:7; Ps 45:12; BDB, recalled), and 'beauty' is its standard English in every version consulted. The book already uses 'beauty' for ṣᵉḇî 'ornament, splendour' (overlay tsevi-beauty-isaiah) so that 'glory' stays reserved for kāḇôḏ, and that entry does not claim 'beauty' exclusively. A distinct English word for yōp̄î ('loveliness', 'fairness') was considered and rejected: it would be less exact than 'beauty' for the plain word, would break the famous and universal rendering of 33:17, and would also require revising the stable 3:24. The two nouns do not stand in the same verse anywhere in Isaiah, so the shared English hides no contrast the Hebrew draws; the overlap is recorded so that a reader can audit it. The claim is direct because 'beauty' is the lexical gloss.

entry.translit: ʾĕnôš (33:8 lōʾ ḥāšaḇ ʾĕnôš; 13:12 ʾôqîr ʾĕnôš; 24:6 wᵉnišʾar ʾĕnôš mizʿār)
entry.strongs: H582 (ʾĕnôš). Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entry.lemma: ʾĕnôš 'human being, mortal; humankind' (poetic generic noun)
entry.wohChoice: 'mortal(s)' for ʾĕnôš used as a substantive in Isaiah: 33:8 'he regards no mortal'; 13:12 'I will make a mortal rarer than fine gold' and 24:6 'few mortals are left' (both stable, already so printed). Context clauses (stable lines, not reopened): attributive 'human' in lᵉḇaḇ ʾĕnôš 'every human heart' (13:7); the idiom ḥereṭ ʾĕnôš 'the pen of a man' (8:1), i.e. ordinary script. Expected later sites of the substantive rule (not yet in appliesTo; their Editors apply or record a departure): 51:7, 51:12, 56:2. Not governed by adam-humankind-ish-man-isaiah, which covers ʾāḏām and ʾîš.
entry.rationale: ʾĕnôš is a poetic generic noun for the human being, often with a nuance of weakness and mortality (Ps 8:5; 90:3; 103:15; BDB; HALOT; recalled). Wave I-4 rule 13 makes generic human nouns gender-neutral, and the stable chapters already render ʾĕnôš as a substantive by 'mortal' (13:12, beside ʾāḏām 'a human being') and 'mortals' (24:6), the rendering NJPS also uses at 33:8 ('Mortal man'). The Translator's 'he regards no one' was gender-neutral but dropped the noun, so the reader could not see that the oppressor's contempt is for human beings as such; 'no mortal' keeps the noun and the book's existing English. The renderings are standard lexical glosses with no interpretive load, so the claim is direct. Orchestrator: ISA-13:12 and ISA-24:6 are in stable chapters; their English lines are unchanged, and their glossaryRefs need this id when the diff is merged.

rationaleAppend: Wave I-5 (Isa 33): extended to 33:1 as the entry asked. The forms are vocative participles with second-person address and finite verbs, so the line reads 'Woe to you, destroyer, who were not destroyed, and treacherous one, with whom they did not deal treacherously! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed; when you have made an end of dealing treacherously, they will deal treacherously with you' (ASV 'destroyest … dealest treacherously'; JPS 1917 'spoilest'; NJPS 'ravager … betrayer'; all checked 2026-11-26). The hapax kannᵉlōṯᵉḵā is read with ASV ('made an end', klh); JPS 1917 'weary' (lʾh) is in commentary.
Wave I-5 (Isa 33): 'Woe to you, destroyer' at 33:1, before the participle šôḏēḏ, with ASV and JPS 1917 ('Woe to thee'); NJPS has 'Ha' (checked 2026-11-26).

Wave I-5 (Isa 33): chapter title 'Isaiah 33 — Woe to the destroyer: who can dwell with the devouring fire, the king in his beauty, and Zion's tent that shall not be moved' (Translator's descriptive title, kept).

Wave I-5 (Isa 33): MT is translated where ASV and NJPS emend. Two sites depart from ASV: 33:2 zᵉrōʿām 'their arm' (ASV 'our arm', presupposing zᵉrōʿēnû; JPS 1917 and NJPS 'their arm') and 33:6 ʾôṣārô 'his treasure' (ASV 'thy treasure'; JPS 1917 'His'; NJPS 'her', noting 'Heb. his'); all checked 2026-11-26. Emendations and variants reported in commentary only: 33:1 the NJPS passives at 21:2 by comparison with this verse; 33:7 'the Arielites' (NJPS, 'a few manuscripts') and the repointing 'I will appear to them'; 33:8 1QIsaᵃ 'a pact' for ʿārîm (known only from the NJPS note; scroll not consulted) and 'an obligation' for ʾĕnôš (NJPS note); 33:11 'my breath' (NJPS); 33:12 'brambles' (NJPS note); 33:17 'perfection of beauty' (NJPS note); 33:23 'even a blind man shall divide much spoil' (NJPS note). Orchestrator: add '33:2 their arm; 33:6 his treasure' to the wohChoice list of MT-over-ASV sites and the 33:8 1QIsaᵃ reading to the variant list.

Wave I-5 (Isa 33): 'beauty' is also the book's English for yōp̄î (33:17 'the king in his beauty'; stable 3:24 'branding instead of beauty'), recorded in overlay yofi-beauty-isaiah. The two nouns never share an Isaiah verse, so the overlap hides no contrast; an Editor who meets both in one verse must separate them.
Wave I-5 (Isa 33): the sail exception applied at 33:23, 'they could not spread the sail' (ASV and JPS 1917 'the sail'; NJPS 'a sail'; checked 2026-11-26).
Wave I-5 (Isa 33): tent context clause applied at 33:20, 'whose stakes shall never be pulled up' (ASV and JPS 1917 'stakes'; NJPS 'pegs'; checked 2026-11-26).

Wave I-5 (Isa 33): nilʿaḡ lāšôn at 33:19 is 'of a stammering tongue', the same English root as laʿăḡê śāp̄āh 'stammering lips' at 28:11 (ruling 7). JPS 1917 'Of a stammering tongue' and NJPS 'So stammering of tongue' have the same word; ASV has 'of a strange tongue' (all checked 2026-11-26). The Translator's 'strange' is replaced.
